summary: This joint resolution nullifies the Bureau of Land Management's November 2024 Buffalo Field Office Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan Amendment by declaring it disapproved under the Congressional Review Act and without legal force.

scores.thoughts: The bill is a Congressional Review Act resolution disapproving a specific BLM resource management plan. It contains no provisions related to federal budgets, appropriations, or spending levels.
The bill does not address tax policy, rates, credits, or revenue measures in any way.
No provisions in the bill relate to healthcare delivery, insurance, public coverage, or market-based reforms.
The legislation has zero connection to firearms regulation or Second Amendment issues.
The bill does not mention immigration, border policy, visas, or enforcement.
No content in the bill pertains to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The resolution concerns BLM land management and has no bearing on military or defense budgets or policy.

The bill uses the CRA to nullify a Bureau of Land Management resource management plan amendment. BLM plans directly govern land use, resource extraction, and environmental restrictions on federal lands. Disapproving the plan prevents the implementation of whatever regulatory framework the BLM adopted, which in practice limits environmental protections in favor of greater resource development flexibility.
The bill contains nothing related to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net policies.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or school choice.
The legislation has no connection to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
The bill does not address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No trade, tariffs, or globalization provisions are present.
The resolution does not address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
The bill has no provisions concerning LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No foreign aid or international assistance measures are included.
The legislation does not touch on voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight provisions exist.
The bill does not address labor law, union rights, or workplace regulations.
No content relates to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination protections.
